about: Amario is the house amaro of Alta Gradazione, a small liqueur company founded in Rome in 2017 by four friends who shared a love of well-made liqueurs and a curiosity about new flavours. One of them, Giacomo, was the first to commit full time, leaving a job at a large consulting firm to get the project going. Their aim is to revive Italian liqueur-making by reworking the classics with a modern hand.

Production is artisanal and in small batches, built on family recipes and natural ingredients, local where possible. Amario infuses more than twenty roots and herbs, led by rhubarb and gentian, with wormwood, eucalyptus, cardamom and galangal among them. Its amber colour comes from molasses rather than caramel colouring, and it is bottled at a fairly sturdy 35%.

The importer describes a sharp, dry, woody bitterness, with rhubarb and gentian up front, a wormwood bite and a cool thread of eucalyptus. Cardamom lingers, and the finish turns spicy and pungent, with pepper and ginger over a discreet sweetness. It works as an after-dinner digestivo, served cold or over ice, and holds its own in bitter-leaning cocktails.
